note: Annual election of one councillor in each of the 15 wards of Belfast Corporation (the member retiring in rotation), nominations Friday 5 January, poll Monday 15 January 1934. Thirteen members were returned unopposed (ten Unionists, two Nationalists and a Labour member); Dock and Pottinger were contested, and Labour took Dock (Belfast News-Letter, 6 and 16 January 1934). State of the Council afterwards: Unionists 45, Nationalists 7, Labour 5, Independents 3. Collier took the place of Councillor A. S. Handforth, who retired. Poll about 45 per cent.
correctionNote: The PRONI register staging (Nov 2026) changed Robert Getgood's vote to 5,013, as the Belfast Corporation register of members (PRONI LA/7/1/CA/1/3) records it. It is restored to the printed 3,013 (proni-items and council-audit, Nov 2026), read on the page image of the Belfast News-Letter, 16 January 1934, p. 7: the paper's majority of 2,980, its 9,006 valid votes and its turnout of "only 45 per cent" of 19,751 electors all require 3,013, so the register's 5,013 is a slip of the pen.
